title: 心理与学习讲座词汇
goal: 辨认心理与学习词汇；听懂实验条件与观察结果。

points.label: 听懂实验条件与观察结果

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 心理与学习词汇和听力材料规格

body.p: 学习行为研究常比较注意、记忆、反馈和习惯。听实验报道时，要分清参加者做了什么、研究者测量了什么、研究者怎样解释结果。

body.box: Researchers counted the words participants recalled. They suggested that a pause might have helped attention.

body.p: counted the words 是测量，might have helped attention 是可能的解释。解释还需要证据支持。

body.box: In a fictional experiment, two groups learned the same list of names. One group received a reminder before a recall test; the other did not. Researchers counted the names recalled by each participant. The reminder group recalled more names on average. The researchers suggested that the reminder may have directed attention to the list, but attention itself was not measured.

body.p: reminder 是两组条件的差异，names recalled 是观察指标。directed attention 是研究者的解释，实验没有直接测量注意力。

body.box:
What did the researchers measure?
1. The number of names recalled by participants
2. Every participant's level of attention
3. The number of lists learned by each group
4. The time spent designing the reminder

body.p: counted the names recalled by each participant 对应第一项。

groups.fill: A group is learning a new set of words. The stud{ents} first re{ad} the li{st} and th{en} recall t{he} words wit{hout} looking ba{ck} at pa{ge} five. They rec{ord} their ans{wers} and compare them with the original list. This comparison gives them feedback on which words they remembered. A later review can address the words that were missed. The number recalled is an observable result; it does not by itself explain why a particular word was remembered.
notes: back：look back at 表示回看。
answers：指回忆词汇时写下的答案。

lines.text: In a fictional study, two groups learned the same set of unfamiliar symbols. One group received feedback immediately after each answer. The other received feedback after the whole set. Researchers recorded how many answers were correct on a later test. The immediate-feedback group answered more items correctly on average. The researchers suggested that prompt corrections might help learners notice errors, but they did not observe what participants noticed. Both groups received the same corrections; their timing differed.

options: The same set of unfamiliar symbols
Different sets of unfamiliar symbols
The corrections given after the whole set
How to notice errors in their answers
items.why: two groups learned the same set of unfamiliar symbols 对应第一项。

items.stem: What differed between the two groups?
options: The symbols presented during learning
The timing of the feedback they received
The corrections contained in the feedback
The kind of test they took later
items.why: immediately after each answer 与 after the whole set 的差别是反馈时间，即第二项。

items.stem: What did the researchers record on the later test?
options: How soon feedback followed each answer
How many corrections each group received
The number of answers that were correct
Which errors each learner noticed
items.why: recorded how many answers were correct 对应第三项。

items.stem: What was observed about the immediate-feedback group?
options: Every participant noticed all errors during learning.
The group received a different set of corrections.
The group answered fewer items correctly on average.
The group answered more items correctly on average.
items.why: answered more items correctly on average 对应第四项。

items.stem: Why is noticing errors an interpretation?
options: The study did not observe what participants noticed.
The groups received their feedback at the same time.
The corrections given to each group were different.
The groups learned different sets of symbols.
items.why: they did not observe what participants noticed 说明该解释未被直接观察，即第一项。

groups.fill: A class is practicing how to remember names. Each stu{dent} reads a li{st} and la{ter} writes t{he} names fr{om} memory. The tea{cher} then che{cks} each ans{wer} and gi{ves} brief feed{back} about mistakes. Students can use that information when they review the names. The exercise records which names were recalled, while the feedback identifies differences between an answer and the list. A correct answer shows what was written on this occasion; it does not reveal every mental process involved.

lines.text: Today I'll describe a fictional experiment about the timing of review. The question was whether two arrangements of the same review time were associated with different results on a later test. The study did not compare review with no review. All participants had the same amount of time available for the task. The researchers prepared a list of unfamiliar object names and their pictures. Participants first studied the complete list. They were then assigned to one of two groups. The first group reviewed the list twice in a single session. The second group reviewed it once in that session and once the following day. Each review used the same list and lasted the same length of time. Two days after the first session, both groups took the same test. Participants saw the pictures and wrote the corresponding names. The researchers counted the number of names each participant supplied correctly. In the fictional results, the second group recalled more names on average. That result describes the difference in scores on this test. The team suggested that the interval between reviews might have helped participants retrieve the information again after some time had passed. The experiment did not directly measure that proposed mental process. It also did not show whether the same arrangement would work equally well for every kind of material. The two groups used one list of object names, and the test was held at one point after the first session. A later study might use different materials and test memory after several intervals. Another distinction concerns time. The groups spent the same total time reviewing, but the time was distributed differently. An account that says the second group studied longer would therefore misstate the condition. The researchers also avoided assuming that every participant in the second group outperformed every participant in the first. The finding concerned the group averages. Some individual scores overlapped. The study illustrates how a comparison can hold the material and total review time constant while changing the spacing of review. Its observed measure was the number of names correctly supplied. The suggested role of retrieval was an explanation, and its validity would require further evidence. Together, the conditions, the measured scores, and the limits describe what the comparison can and cannot establish.

items.stem: What was held constant for the two review groups?
options: The length of the gap between the two reviews
The total review time and the list being studied
The average number of names that each group recalled
The number of reviews held in the first session
items.why: same list 和 same total time reviewing 表明材料与总复习时间相同，即第二项。

options: The pictures used in the final test
The number of object names on the study list
The total number of review sessions
The spacing of the two review sessions
items.why: twice in a single session 与 once ... the following day 表明两次复习的间隔不同，即第四项。

items.stem: What did the researchers measure on the later test?
options: The number of names correctly written for pictures
The exact mental process behind every correct answer
The time each participant spent on review
The number of names each participant reviewed
items.why: counted the number of names each participant supplied correctly 对应第一项。

items.stem: What did the fictional results show?
options: Every individual in the second group scored higher.
The first group studied for twice as long in total.
The second group recalled more names on average.
The groups received different lists of object names.
items.why: the second group recalled more names on average 对应第三项。

items.stem: Why is the role of retrieval described as an explanation?
options: The researchers directly observed every act of retrieval.
The proposed mental process was not directly measured.
Some individual scores in the two groups overlapped.
The groups spent different amounts of time reviewing.
items.why: The experiment did not directly measure that proposed mental process 表明检索作用是解释，即第二项。
